g.text: Rendered evidence from captured output
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-556-* **Suite accuracy** — pass rate of the most recent run, with the last three runs' trend so yo
u can see whether you're improving or regressing.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:557:* **Run insights** — an AI-written diff against your previous completed run: which cases moved
, which tools changed behavior, which models diverged. Skim this first; it usually points at the right rabbit hole. The model pass
is **included with MCPJam and consumes no credits**; it counts against a daily insight quota shared with swarm wave and user-test
ing insights. Guests browsing without a signed-in account will see a **Sign in** prompt in the insights band — signing in unlocks
the feature without losing your place.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-558-* **Overview tab** — every run with its summary metrics, plus a Suite Health chart whose bars
link to individual run rows. Click in for the iteration-level breakdown. The table shows **Date** first, then **Run**, with separa
te **Client**, **Model**, **Platform**, **Commit**, **Rate**, **Latency**, **Tokens**, and **Calls** columns. The Client column co
unts unique clients; when there are more than two, a **+N** badge appears — hover it to see all clients in a tooltip.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-559-* **Cases tab** — every case with its latest verdict and a quick replay button. To delete a ca
se, hover its row and click the trash icon; a confirmation dialog appears before the case is removed. The trash icon is hidden for
CI-managed suites and read-only configurations. You can also delete the open case from the case editor header using the same tras
h icon — it is hidden for unsaved drafts.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-560-* **Executions tab** — a flat, filterable list of every individual test execution across all c
ases, sorted most-recent-first. Each row shows the case name, result (passed/failed/pending/cancelled), and timestamp. Click any r
ow to open it in the compare view.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-592-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-593-#### Cross-host matrix
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-594-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:595:When two or more host configurations are attached to a suite, a **By case / By host** toggle a
ppears. **By host** shows a matrix — one column per host, one row per case. Each cell shows pass/fail dots, pass rate, median late
ncy, and token usage. A host detached after runs were recorded stays visible, labelled **historical**.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-596-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:597:### Cost
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-598-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:599:Every iteration carries the MCPJam-billed cost of the model work it did,
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-600-priced when the trial finished and stamped with the rates used — so a run's
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:601:cost does not move later when prices change. It rolls up onto cases, runs and
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-602-the metric strip.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-603-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:604:A dash (`—`) means **no cost was observed**, never that the trial was free:
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-605-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-606-| Why | What you see |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-607-| - | - |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:608:| Your own API key (BYOK) | MCPJam did not bill it, so there is no cost to report. |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:609:| A harness run (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) | A harness turn mixes models — sub-agents on che
aper models under a main one — and the trial's totals carry no per-model split, so no honest single figure exists. Harness cost ar
rives with billed attribution. |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:610:| No token usage reported | Nothing to price. |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-611-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:612:A cost your own SDK runner reported is shown but labelled **runner** — it is
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-613-real, but MCPJam neither computed nor verified it.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-614-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-615-When only some of a run's trials were priced, the total says so. That
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-616-distinction matters most in CI: a run that looks cheaper may simply be a run
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-617-we priced less of, which is why the compare API reports coverage counts
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:618:alongside the cost and a cost gate treats partial coverage as non-gateable
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-619-rather than as a pass.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-620-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-621-### Run view
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-639-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-640-For CI-managed (SDK) suites, clicking a test name still opens the definition in read-only mode
— configuration edits remain locked, but you can inspect the prompt and checks.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-641-
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md:642:* **Per-iteration row** with case, model, pass/fail, tokens, cost, duration, and the tool call
s that actually happened. Each row also shows a one-line summary of where that trial's user-value chain stopped — for example `bro
ke at Tool response`, `Request satisfied`, or `chain withheld` — so you can scan the table without opening each row.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-643-* **Expected vs actual** tool calls side-by-side when an iteration fails. For failed iteration
s, a **Categorized diff** above the raw Expected/Actual grids groups discrepancies into four categories:
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-644- * **Missing** — expected tool calls that were never made
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/evals.md-645- * **Extra** — actual calls that weren't expected (reported but non-fatal by default)
